stories.title: Blackstone, LBA Land $270M Office Refi in L.A.’s Culver City
stories.excerpt: Blackstone and LBA Realty are set to close a $270 million commercial mortgage-backed securities refinancing for an office campus in Southern California’s Culver City. Nomura Holdings, which is part of Japan’s largest investment bank, and brokerage Nomura Group will provide the loan for One Culver, a 378,377-square-foot property at 10000 Washington Boulevard. Traded first reported the loan. One Culver includes office space, three soundstages, retail shops, restaurants and an Equinox gym. The campus sits adjacent to Sony Pictures Studios, and near Amazon Studios and Sony Pictures Animation. Blackstone and Nomura both did not immediately respond to a requests for comment. The refinancing is expected to retire $310 million in existing debt and cover approximately $5.8 million in closing costs. The financing comes more than four years after Blackstone partnered with LBA to recapitalize the property in a deal valued at more than $500 million. Blackstone holds a 90 percent stake in One Culver. LBA had acquired the property for $159 million in 2014 before completing a Gensler-designed renovation in 2017. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Blackstone/LBA refinance $270M office campus at One Culver, Culver City, CA
Mixed-use property includes 378K SF office, soundstages, retail; adjacent Sony Pictures Studios
Refinance retires $310M existing debt; property previously recapitalized at $500M+ valuation
stories.summary: Blackstone and LBA Realty closed a $270 million CMBS refinancing for One Culver, a 378,377-square-foot mixed-use campus in Culver City anchored by office, soundstages, and retail near Sony Studios. Nomura Holdings provided the loan, retiring $310 million in existing debt. The property was recapitalized by the partners in 2020 at a $500 million-plus valuation; Blackstone holds a 90% stake.
stories.impact: Office asset refinancing in media/entertainment submarket signals lender appetite for stabilized mixed-use properties with entertainment tenancy, but offers limited direct signal for multifamily demand. Culver City's media cluster growth (Amazon, Sony) supports broader Los Angeles talent in-migration, indirectly supporting rental demand in adjacent residential markets.

stories.title: New Tenants Bring DivcoWest’s Hudson Square AI Hub to Full Occupancy
stories.excerpt: DivcoWest announced 325 Hudson St., a multitenant AI tech hub in Hudson Square, has reached 100% occupancy following recent leasing activity. The last remaining space in the 10-story, 220,000-square-foot building was taken up by Flourish, an AI startup, Moment, an AI partner for investment management, and a life sciences enterprise currently in stealth mode. “AI innovators are not just settling in San Francisco. New York is clearly the second most popular market in the country with 2.8 million square feet of active AI demand,” said Gregg Walker, president, DivcoWest Real Estate Asset Management. Paul Amrich, Neil King, Brooke Dewing, and Kelly Tipton of CBRE represented DivcoWest, with Bill Harvey, John Cahill, and Thomas Burrus of JLL serving as life science advisors. Moment was represented by Josh Berg of Newmark. Flourish was represented by Billy Janetschek, Nicholas Hein, and Matthew Derose of Nomad. The stealth life science tenant was represented by David Stockel and Taylor Walker of CBRE. The post New Tenants Bring DivcoWest’s Hudson Square AI Hub to Full Occupancy appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: DivcoWest's Hudson Square AI hub reaches 100% occupancy; 220K SF, 10-story building
Flourish, Moment AI startups + unnamed life sciences stealth tenant complete leasing
NYC has 2.8M SF active AI demand; second only to San Francisco
stories.summary: DivcoWest announced 325 Hudson Street in Manhattan's Hudson Square reached full occupancy following leases from AI startups Flourish and Moment, plus a stealth life sciences tenant. The 220,000-square-foot, 10-story multitenant tech hub is now fully let. DivcoWest noted NYC has 2.8 million square feet of active AI demand, positioning it as the country's second-largest AI hub after San Francisco.
stories.impact: Manhattan's emergence as a competitive AI hub signals sustained white-collar job and talent inflow to NYC, driving sustained rental demand for multifamily in close-proximity submarkets (Hudson Square, Tribeca, East Village). Expect rent growth and absorption acceleration in CBD-adjacent residential neighborhoods as tech talent clusters consolidate; development near transit is increasingly defensible.

stories.title: Galvanize Adds Orange County Industrial to Expanding Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Galvanize Real Estate (GRE), the sustainable real estate strategy of Galvanize, has acquired a three-property, 280,000-square-foot industrial portfolio located in Orange County. The transaction marks GRE’s second California acquisition and fifth acquisition nationwide in the past year, bringing the strategy’s total portfolio to 3.8 million square feet. “We view Orange County, with its strategic location, diversified economy, and limited new supply, as particularly well suited to our industrial strategy,” said Rachel Reardon, managing director, acquisitions at GRE. “Acquiring our first assets in Southern California allows GRE to capitalize on favorable market fundamentals while seeking to create value through decarbonization.” As with GRE’s recent acquisition in the Bay Area, the business plan for the OC portfolio includes upgrading the properties with behind-the-meter solar energy generation, battery storage, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure. The portfolio’s planned on-site renewable energy program is expected to generate approximately 475 MWh of clean electricity annually. The post Galvanize Adds Orange County Industrial to Expanding Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Galvanize Real Estate acquires 280K SF industrial portfolio in Orange County, CA
OC limited supply, strategic logistics location; GRE's second California deal this year
Portfolio includes solar, battery storage, EV charging infrastructure; 475 MWh annual generation
stories.summary: Galvanize Real Estate acquired a three-property, 280,000-square-foot industrial portfolio in Orange County, marking its second California deal and fifth acquisition nationwide in the past year (total portfolio now 3.8M SF). The business plan includes installing behind-the-meter solar, battery storage, and EV charging across the properties to generate approximately 475 MWh of clean electricity annually.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Orange County industrial scarcity and investor appetite for supply-constrained logistics assets is a positive signal for industrial rents, but does not materially affect residential demand drivers or capital competition for apartment development in the region.

stories.title: Long Island City Redevelopment Site Trades to Queens Developer
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap recently closed the sale of 49-03 Fifth St., a redevelopment site in Long Island City. The asset sold for $6.1 million. “The depth of the buyer pool in Long Island City is as strong as we have seen it,” said Sean Fopeano in Marcus & Millichap’s New York City office. “Developers remain extremely bullish on both the condo and rental markets. That confidence, combined with a limited number of remaining sites, continues to push land pricing to all-time highs.” Fopeano, Shaun Riney and David Cornejo of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property on behalf of the private family seller. They also procured the buyer, a Queens developer. The property is a single commercial unit on a 0.11-acre lot featuring approximately 10,000 square feet of unused air rights. It is situated within an M1-4/R6A zoning district, offering redevelopment opportunities in a mixed-use district. The post Long Island City Redevelopment Site Trades to Queens Developer appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Long Island City redevelopment site (49-03 Fifth St.) trades for $6.1M to Queens developer
0.11-acre lot with 10K SF air rights; M1-4/R6A zoning enables mixed-use
Broker noted 'depth of buyer pool' and 'all-time high' land pricing in LIC
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of 49-03 Fifth Street, a 0.11-acre redevelopment site in Long Island City, for $6.1 million to a Queens-based developer. The property features approximately 10,000 square feet of unused air rights within an M1-4/R6A mixed-use zoning district. Brokers noted developer confidence remains high on condo and rental markets, with limited remaining sites driving land prices to all-time highs.
stories.impact: Long Island City land market remains extremely tight and competitive; all-time pricing signals scarcity of developable sites and robust developer demand for rental and condo projects. Limited available inventory pushes risk onto timing and underwriting precision—developers must move quickly on acquisition but face severe cost pressures, compressing margins in an environment of elevated construction and financing costs.

stories.title: Sprouts-Anchored Retail Sells to California Gold Development
stories.excerpt: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors arranged the $9.3-million sale of a Sprouts‑anchored retail property, which includes a 21,000‑square‑foot junior box lease‑up opportunity. The property is located in Victorville, one of the fastest‑growing markets in Southern California. SVP Sean Cox and EVP Kevin Fryman represented both the seller and the buyer. The seller was a private advisory and investment firm based in Los Angeles, while the buyer, California Gold Development Corp., a private commercial real estate investment and development company and repeat client of Hanley, is headquartered in Sonora. “This property checks every box: a top‑performing Sprouts, a junior box lease‑up opportunity, freeway visibility, and a dense trade area that continues to grow,” said Fryman. “The buyer engaged a national tenant during escrow, creating an opportunity for them to execute a lease during escrow.” The property is located at 12450 Amargosa Rd. within Village Center, a 350,000‑square‑foot community center. The post Sprouts-Anchored Retail Sells to California Gold Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sprouts-anchored retail property sells for $9.3M in Victorville, CA; 21K SF junior box available
Victorville is fastest-growing Southern California market; strong trade area density
Buyer, California Gold Development, secured national tenant lease during escrow
stories.summary: Hanley Investment Group arranged the $9.3 million sale of a Sprouts-anchored retail property in Victorville, California, which includes a 21,000-square-foot junior box lease-up opportunity. Victorville is one of the fastest-growing markets in Southern California. The buyer, California Gold Development, secured a national tenant lease during escrow, de-risking the junior box component.
stories.impact: Victorville's rapid growth (population, logistics, labor in-migration) is a leading indicator of sustained multifamily demand in the Inland Empire submarket. Retail anchoring and tenant demand confirm employment and household formation are underway; multifamily developers should evaluate Victorville and surrounding Mojave Desert corridors for apartment development before land costs and competition escalate further.

stories.title: Qube Inks 52K-SF Deal at Related and Oxford’s 70 Hudson Yards Development
stories.excerpt: Related Companies and Oxford Properties’ 70 Hudson Yards — a roughly 1.4 million-square-foot office tower that won’t be complete until 2028 — has secured another office tenant, Commercial Observer has learned. Qube, a global investment manager, has agreed to lease 52,000 square feet at the planned 52-story office building currently under development in Manhattan’s Hudson Yards, according to a source with knowledge of the deal and confirmed by Avison Young’s third-quarter Manhattan office report. The length of the lease and the asking rent were unclear, but Avison Young’s report found office asking rents in Hudson Yards averaged $117.66 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026. It’s also unclear who brokered the deal. Spokespeople for Related, Oxford, Avison Young and Qube did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Qube currently has a New York City office listed across the street at 50 Hudson Yards and will likely relocate once the new 70 Hudson Yards tower is complete. News of the Qube deal comes after financial advisory firm Deloitte signed a lease in April 2025 to anchor 70 Hudson Yards with 800,000 square feet, as CO previously reported. That deal was signed long before the planned tower between West 35th and West 36th streets broke ground in June 2025. Deloitte will consolidate its current offices — including its current HQ at 30 Rockefeller Plaza — into its new space at 70 Hudson Yards. Once complete, the new tower will feature event spaces, private dining areas, a podcast studio and an 8,000-square-foot terrace. Related and Oxford’s megaproject in Hudson Yards, designed by Roger Ferris + Partners and Gensler, is planned as New York City’s first zero-carbon-emission skyscraper and represents one of the largest ground-up office developments in the U.S. since the COVID pandemic. bullets: Qube (global investment manager) leases 52K SF at Related/Oxford's 70 Hudson Yards, Manhattan
52-story office tower, 1.4M SF total; completion not until 2028; asking rents $117.66/SF avg
Qube relocating from existing NYC office; pre-leasing validates Hudson Yards demand
stories.summary: Qube, a global investment manager, has agreed to lease 52,000 square feet at 70 Hudson Yards, a 1.4 million-square-foot, 52-story office tower under development by Related Companies and Oxford Properties in Manhattan's Hudson Yards. The building is not expected to be complete until 2028. Average asking rents in Hudson Yards averaged $117.66 per square foot in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Hudson Yards office pre-leasing demonstrates continued demand for class-A Manhattan office space despite market skepticism; sustained financial services and professional services job clusters support this corridor. Multifamily developers should monitor Hudson Yards office recovery closely—white-collar in-migration and office occupancy anchor residential demand in surrounding Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen, and Midtown West submarkets, justifying near-term rental deliveries.

stories.title: Owner-User Acquires NJ Cold Storage Facility
stories.excerpt: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the $6-million sale of 609 10th St., an industrial and cold storage facility in Union City, NJ. The firm’s Andrew Schwartz, Jordan Sobel, André Balthazard and Dan Bottiglieri represented both the seller, 10th St Realty, LLC, and the buyer, PanRaj Holding, LLC. “609 10th St. presented a compelling opportunity for an owner-user to acquire a vacant industrial facility in an exceptionally supply-constrained location, which is just minutes from Midtown Manhattan,” said Sobel. “The property’s existing infrastructure, functional layout and connectivity to the entire New York Metro region made it particularly well suited for the buyer’s needs.” Located on a 0.81-acre site, 609 10th St. features 33,515 square feet of industrial space on the ground floor, with additional second floor and basement space, bringing the total usable area to 42,451 square feet. The facility includes cold storage, manufacturing, dry storage and office space, as well as interior loading docks and multiple drive-in doors. The post Owner-User Acquires NJ Cold Storage Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Owner-user acquires 42.5K SF cold storage/industrial facility in Union City, NJ for $6M
0.81-acre site with cold storage, manufacturing, dry storage, loading docks; 33 min to Manhattan
Supply-constrained industrial market in NJ; functional layout drives value for user
stories.summary: Cushman & Wakefield arranged the $6 million sale of 609 10th Street, a 42,451-square-foot industrial and cold storage facility in Union City, New Jersey, to owner-user PanRaj Holding. The 0.81-acre property features cold storage, manufacturing, dry storage, and office space, plus interior loading docks and drive-in doors. Union City's proximity to Midtown Manhattan (minutes) and supply constraints made the functional layout particularly attractive.
stories.impact: Union City/North Jersey industrial scarcity and owner-user acquisition strength signal tight regional logistics supply and end-user demand for warehouse and cold storage. Limited direct multifamily impact, but strong industrial occupancy and user absorption near Manhattan confirms job density and commuter flows into NYC—supporting rental demand in northern New Jersey and Queens residential markets.

stories.title: Alcion Ventures, Slate Offload 60 East 12th Street for $83M
stories.excerpt: A joint venture of Alcion Ventures and Slate Property Group is parting ways with a rental apartment building near Manhattan’s Union Square at a loss, Commercial Observer has learned. The JV, using the entity 60 East 12th Street Owner, has sold the 133-unit 60 East 12th Street to Stonehenge Investment and Wraith Capital Group for $82.5 million, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. The sale price is a roughly 23.3 percent discount from the $107.5 million Alcion and Slate bought the property for in an off-market deal from Heller Realty in 2019. Alcion has a 91 percent stake in the site, while Slate holds a 9 percent stake. Built in 1962, the 13-story 60 East 12th Street has a mix of apartments ranging from studios to three-bedrooms and includes 5,100 square feet of ground-level retail space, all of which seems to be currently occupied by an attached Metropolis parking garage. No brokers were involved in the new sale, according to the source. It’s unclear what Stonehenge and Wraith Capital are planning for the property between Broadway and Fourth Avenue, but the building will likely remain residential, as Stonehenge manages and invests in multifamily assets in New York City. Spokespeople for Alcion, Slate, Stonehenge and Wraith Capital did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The sale comes as Alcion winds down its operations and liquidates its assets, the source said. The Boston-based real estate private equity firm was founded in 2005 and focuses on value-add and opportunistic investments across the U.S. Alcion has been on a selling streak of its properties in recent years, including several residential and mixed-use properties in Brooklyn. Last year, Alcion and Golub & Company also listed One East Delaware, a 37-story apartment tower in Chicago, on the market after purchasing it for $146 million in 2016, The Real Deal reported. bullets: Alcion Ventures/Slate sell 133-unit Manhattan apartment at Union Square for $82.5M; 23.3% loss

stories.summary: A joint venture of Alcion Ventures and Slate Property Group sold 60 East 12th Street, a 133-unit apartment building near Union Square in Manhattan, to Stonehenge Investment and Wraith Capital Group for $82.5 million. The sale represents a 23.3% discount from the $107.5 million purchase price in 2019. The 13-story building includes studios to three-bedroom units and 5,100 square feet of ground-floor retail space.
stories.impact: Significant loss on apartment sale suggests multifamily valuation compression in Manhattan's East Village despite neighborhood prime location and walkability. Indicates that acquisition timing (2019 pre-pandemic peak), rising operating costs, and refinancing challenges have eroded equity for value-add operators. Signals caution on Manhattan rental basis costs and underwriting assumptions in transitional economic environments; developers should stress-test hold-period financing and exit scenarios in mature urban markets.

stories.title: Multifamily Investment Firm Bozzuto Relocating HQ in Maryland
stories.excerpt: Bozzuto is moving its corporate headquarters from Greenbelt, Md., to Maple Lawn in Howard County about 45 minutes north after signing a 57,837-square-foot office lease at the 605-acre mixed-use community. The real estate development, construction and management company announced Wednesday that it will occupy two and a half floors at 8160 Maple Lawn Boulevard in Fulton, Md., and plans to move about 225 employees there during the first quarter of 2027. Bozzuto will also keep its Greenbelt office as a corporate services hub. Maple Lawn is a partnership between Greenebaum Enterprises and St. John Properties. The community includes more than 1,300 homes, over 1.8 million square feet of commercial space and more than 215,000 square feet of retail. “The wide range of walkable amenities, including restaurants, shops, grocery, recreation and an onsite hotel are extremely attractive to businesses seeking to provide the best work environment for their employees,” Matt Lenihan, executive vice president for St. John Properties, said in a statement. Bozzuto manages about 150,000 apartments, employs nearly 5,000 people and has $3.5 billion in combined construction and development pipelines. “We know firsthand that the right environment shapes how people connect, collaborate and thrive,” Bozzuto CEO and President Toby Bozzuto said in a statement. Bozzuto is also preparing to relocate its Northern Virginia office. Once both moves are complete, the company will have five corporate offices across the Washington, D.C., region, and 10 nationwide, including a new office in Seattle. St. John Properties Vice President Bill Jautze represented the landlord in the transaction. CBRE’s David Fields and Charlie Carroccio, along with Stream Realty’s Lou Christopher, represented Bozzuto. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bozzuto relocates HQ from Greenbelt to Maple Lawn, Howard County, MD; 225 employees
57.8K SF lease at 8160 Maple Lawn Boulevard; move planned Q1 2027
Maple Lawn: 605-acre mixed-use community; 1,300+ homes, 1.8M+ SF commercial space
stories.summary: Bozzuto, a multifamily real estate development, construction, and management company, is relocating its corporate headquarters from Greenbelt, Maryland, to Maple Lawn in Howard County, signing a 57,837-square-foot lease on two and a half floors at 8160 Maple Lawn Boulevard in Fulton. The company plans to move approximately 225 employees in Q1 2027 while retaining a smaller Greenbelt office. Maple Lawn is a 605-acre mixed-use community developed by Greenebaum Enterprises and St. John Properties, featuring over 1,300 homes, 1.8 million square feet of commercial space, and 215,000 square feet of retail.
stories.impact: Bozzuto's relocation to Maple Lawn—a live-work-play mixed-use environment—signals operator preference for amenity-rich, walkable suburban nodes over isolated office parks. This validates the mixed-use TOD model and suggests sustained talent demand in mixed-use suburban communities. For developers, Maple Lawn's ability to anchor a Fortune 500-tier multifamily operator's HQ indicates strong market fundamentals in the DC exurbs and justifies continued apartment investment along the I-95 corridor in northern Maryland/Howard County.

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz Miami Project’s $1.1B Financing Package Speeds Closer to Completion
stories.excerpt: Ladies and gents, start your engines. Mercedes-Benz Places–Miami’s construction financing is officially off to the races, sources confirmed to Commercial Observer. J.P. Morgan is leading the $1.11 billion financing package for the luxury-branded, mixed-use tower in Miami’s Brickell neighborhood and providing a $860 million construction loan. Nuveen Green Capital is also in the process of providing roughly $250 million in Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) financing for the project. While term sheets have now been signed, the deal has not yet closed. It’s expected to close by year end, sources said. Walker & Dunlop’s Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Sean Reimer and Sean Bastian are negotiating the financing. The Promote first reported news of the mammoth loan being in the works. JDS Development is the original developer behind the Miami project. Fontainebleau Development, led by Jeffrey Soffer, joined as a partner in the deal earlier this year to move the development forward after it became embroiled in a foreclosure suit. Now the two firms are developing the project together. When completed, the 67-story Mercedes-Benz Places-Miami, at 140 SW 11th Street, will include 791 luxury condos, 130,000 square feet of amenities, including a cocktail bar and two restaurants and wellness facilities, 200,000 square feet of office space, a 174-key hotel, a parking garage and a park. Sources said that J.P. Morgan’s loan is collateralized by the entire Mercedes-Benz project, while Nuveen’s will be collateralized by its commercial component only. The German car manufacturer first lent its name to the Brickell tower in 2024, marking Mercedes-Benz’s first branded real estate project in the U.S. It followed the proliferation of towers by competitors Porsche, Aston Martin and Bentley. bullets: Mercedes-Benz Places Miami secures $1.11B financing package; J.P. Morgan lead on $860M construction loan
Nuveen Green Capital providing $250M C-PACE financing; closure expected by year-end
Luxury mixed-use tower in Miami's Brickell; JDS Development original developer
stories.summary: Mercedes-Benz Places, a luxury-branded mixed-use tower in Miami's Brickell neighborhood, secured a $1.11 billion financing package with J.P. Morgan leading a $860 million construction loan and Nuveen Green Capital providing approximately $250 million in C-PACE financing. Term sheets are signed and closure is expected by year-end. JDS Development is the original developer; Fontainebleau is also involved in the project.
stories.impact: Successful close of large, marquee mixed-use construction financing in Miami validates lender appetite for branded luxury residential-office-retail projects despite higher interest rates. Deep capital stack ($250M C-PACE) indicates green/ESG financing availability for major projects. For multifamily developers in South Florida, signals that institutional construction debt remains available for high-quality, mixed-use urban core projects; Brickell multifamily demand remains supported by office, hospitality, and retail anchor tenant pre-leasing and financing momentum.
